## Prime-Agent System Prompt (ACP Template)

For file editing operations, the prime-agent runtime exposes a pre-installed `mcp` Python object with `list_tools` and `call_tool` methods. Use them to discover and invoke tools.

Example discovery and call:

```python
tools_list = await mcp.list_tools("tools")
for t in tools_list:
    print(t["name"], t["inputSchema"])

result = await mcp.call_tool("tools", "ox-bridge-write", {"path": "/tmp/x.py", "content": "# code here"})
print(result)
```

The `tools` MCP server exposes:
- `ox-bridge-write`: write a file (args: `path`, `content`)
- `ox-bridge-edit`: edit a file with hunks (args: `path`, `edits` = [{old, new}])
- `ox-bridge-read`: read a file region (args: `path`, `start`, `end`)

All bridging calls return synchronously. Print results to confirm before proceeding.

BBCode-to-HTML converter with a proper tag stack, not regex soup. /workspace/bbcode: src/index.ts supports [b], [i], [u], [url=target], [quote=author], [code] and [list] with [*] items; a real tokenizer plus stack handles improper nesting by auto-closing (like [b][i]x[/b] closes the i first and reopens nothing, document the rule), unknown or unclosed tags render as literal text, [code] content is fully escaped with inner bbcode ignored, and url targets get the same scheme allowlist treatment as any sanitizer (javascript: becomes plain text). Everything else HTML-escaped. Vitest: nesting auto-close cases with exact expected HTML strings, the code-block literalness, url allowlist, list item splitting, and unclosed-tag fallback. Run npx vitest run until every case passes.

TYPECHECK-OK

Done. All 23 tests pass and the source type-checks under `--strict`. **Files:** - `/workspace/bbcode/src/index.ts` — the converter - `/workspace/bbcode/test/bbcode.test.ts` — vitest suite - `/workspace/bbcode/package.json` **Architecture (no regex soup):** 1. **Tokenizer** — a single linear scanner that emits `text | open{name,attr} | close{name}` tokens. A `[` that doesn't parse as a well-formed tag is left as ordinary text. 2. **Converter** — walks the token stream with an open-element stack. Every pushed element carries the HTML needed to close it. **The documented auto-close rule** (in the file header): a closing tag closes the *nearest* matching open element; anything above it on the stack is auto-closed and **not re-opened**. So `[b][i]x[/b]y` → `xy`. Unclosed tags at EOF close in reverse order; only genuinely unmatched closers (`[/b]` with no opener) fall back to literal text. **Other behaviors:** - **Unknown tags** — `[spoiler]…[/spoiler]` renders entirely as literal text (the closer hits the unmatched-closer fallback). - **`[code]`** — raw mode: consumes verbatim until its `[/code]` (nesting-aware for repeated `[code]`), escaping everything, so inner BBCode is ignored: `[code][b]x[/b] [/code]` → `
[b]x[/b] <s>
`. - **URL allowlist** — same treatment as any sanitizer: schemes checked against `{http, https, mailto, ftp}` (case-insensitive), relative URLs allowed. `javascript:`/`data:`/`vbscript:` targets make the whole tag plain text, and its `[/url]` is swallowed via a stack marker. - **`[list]`/`[*]`** — each `[*]` closes the previous `
  • ` (auto-closing anything nested inside it) and opens a new one; `[*]` outside a list is literal. - Everything else HTML-escaped (`& < > "`). One bug worth mentioning from the build: my first run had all tests failing with empty output because `bbcodeToHtml` passed the raw string where the token array belonged — fixed by tokenizing before constructing the converter.
